0.headline: Razorpay bets on customised AI agents to expand beyond its payments business
0.heading: Razorpay bets on customised AI agents to expand beyond its payments business
0.intro: The Bengaluru-based company is positioning AI agents as a new layer of merchant services, as it looks to tap the growing use of conversational and voice-led commerce.
0.body:
Payments firm Razorpay is expanding its artificial intelligence (AI) offerings beyond transaction processing by deploying agents to help businesses recover abandoned carts, collect overdue EMIs and automate customer interactions.

The company’s AI agent platform, Agent Studio, clocked around five lakh monthly agent runs.

"We are live on 350 brands. As of September, we have done roughly half a million agent runs monthly. The agents are performing tasks for buyers on behalf of a business," Khilan Haria, chief product officer at Razorpay, told Moneycontrol in an interaction.

The company’s rapid deployment of AI-led products comes even as it accelerates its revenue growth ahead of its proposed initial public offering. Earlier this month, Razorpay secured SEBI nod for its $5 billion initial public offering, which could hit the market early next year.

The platform, launched in March this year, lets businesses deploy AI agents for specific tasks, including recovering abandoned shopping carts, collecting overdue loan instalments, sending investment reminders, and following up with customers who drop off during a purchase.

The company did not disclose how many of these brands are paying customers or how much revenue Agent Studio currently generates.

"Our revenue models can sometimes be more aggregated, sometimes blended, sometimes feature-specific. When a customer sees value, they pay for it. So we can capture the value we create for our customers," Haria said.

AI-led voice calls improve conversion rates

One of the applications of Agent Studio that has gained momentum among customers is voice-led commerce, where an AI agent calls a customer on behalf of a business to complete a transaction or recover a payment that would otherwise have been missed.

For instance, a lending company can use an agent to contact a borrower who has missed an EMI, remind them about the pending instalment and facilitate its payment. Similarly, ecommerce businesses can use voice agents to follow up with customers who have added products to their carts but dropped off before completing the purchase.

Haria said conversion rates in some of these use cases were encouraging, although the outcome varied depending on the application.

"I think about 8-10% conversion in most of the scenarios. That's as high conversion for a dropped-off opportunity, because not everyone picks up the call," he said.

The platform is also being used by businesses in the investment sector to remind customers about missed investment activities.

AI is moving beyond customer support

The relatively high conversion rates suggest that businesses are beginning to use AI agents not just to respond to customer queries but also to pursue transactions and recover revenue that might otherwise be lost.

On November 17, Razorpay announced a partnership with Meta to enable payments through Meta Business Agent on WhatsApp, allowing customers to discover products, interact with businesses and complete purchases using UPI, cards or net banking within the same conversation.

“The opportunity is also meaningful if you look at SMBs, who don't get the involvement and are not necessarily capable of taking advantage of this on day one,” Haria said.

The integration extends Razorpay's agentic-commerce strategy to WhatsApp, where millions of Indian businesses already have a high engagement with customers. Unlike Agent Studio, which allows businesses to deploy AI agents for specific workflows, this integration brings Razorpay's payment infrastructure into Meta's conversational shopping experience.

Last month, Razorpay also partnered with OpenAI to help Indian brands advertise on ChatGPT through its growth marketing platform, Engage. The offering allows brands to prepare product catalogues, launch advertising campaigns and track performance on the platform, with an AI agent assisting in campaign management.

Moving beyond payment processing

Razorpay is positioning Agent Studio as a marketplace and builder platform for businesses to deploy specialised AI agents to suit their specific requirements.

The initial set of applications developed on the platform included abandoned-cart recovery, subscription payment recovery, dispute responses and cash-flow forecasting. The platform also allows businesses to build customised agents by describing the tasks they want automated, without having to write code.

“The pre-AI way was chatbots and basic automation and workflows. We are moving beyond that, thanks to the context, the memory and the decision layer that AI enables across the buyer and merchant journey,” Haria said.

In September, Razorpay launched RAY, an AI account manager on WhatsApp. The feature e allows businesses to check payment and settlement information, generate payment links and initiate refunds through messages or voice notes.

The latest adoption numbers indicate that Razorpay is attempting to take the product beyond its initial launch use cases and establish it across a wider set of businesses.

The move is part of a broader strategy by the fintech to become more involved in the day-to-day operations of merchants rather than remain limited to processing their payments.

“We believe both the buyer journey and the merchant journey are going to change significantly with AI,” Haria said, indicating that Razorpay itself wants to be present in helping the merchants move through the AI-led transformation.

A slew of launches

Over the past few months, Razorpay has announced several AI-led initiatives across payments, business banking and customer acquisition.

In June, its business banking platform RazorpayX introduced AI agents for cash-flow insights, receivables and payouts. These tools are designed to help businesses track incoming payments, follow up on unpaid invoices and initiate payouts through conversational instructions, with final approval through an OTP.

In August, the company launched Vulcan, a proprietary transaction-led AI model designed to improve payment routing, fraud detection and checkout personalisation.

The slew of products and features indicates the company increasingly covers different parts of a merchant's business, from accepting payments and managing cash flows to recovering customers and acquiring new ones, while making merchants more dependent on its platform.

According to Haria, four broad categories of this emerging commerce include conversational commerce, price discovery, voice commerce and autonomous commerce.

The first three could see wider adoption as consumers use AI assistants to discover products, compare prices or complete purchases through voice interactions.

However, autonomous commerce, where an agent independently makes purchases on behalf of a consumer, is likely to remain a smaller segment initially.

Haria said the next six to 12 months could see agentic commerce move beyond its early stages and begin appearing in more routine consumer activities.

1.headline: Anthropic eyes world's biggest IPO: Who are the 300 investors set to reap a windfall?
1.heading: Anthropic eyes world's biggest IPO: Who are the 300 investors set to reap a windfall?
1.intro: In 2023, Spark Capital became the first venture capital firm to lead an Anthropic investment, raising $450 million at a $4.5 billion valuation.
1.body:
Amid the turmoil surrounding Nvidia, AI major Anthropic is eyeing what could become the biggest IPO in capital market history. Its planned market debut this week is expected to value the Claude maker at $1.33 trillion or more, according to The Wall Street Journal (WSJ).

Already valued at $965 billion, Anthropic has attracted more than 300 investors, including venture capital firms, private equity funds, angel investors, corporates and sovereign wealth funds, according to PitchBook data cited by the WSJ. Here's how the company built its investor base through successive funding rounds.

Series A and B

In 2021, Anthropic raised $124 million at a valuation of $461 million in a Series A round led by Skype engineer Jaan Tallinn. In 2022, it raised $580 million in Series B funding at a $3 billion valuation, led by Sam Bankman-Fried, then CEO of FTX. His shares were subsequently sold in bankruptcy proceedings.

Series C, D and E

In 2023, Spark Capital became the first venture capital firm to lead an Anthropic investment, raising $450 million at a $4.5 billion valuation. Menlo Ventures led the next round, raising more than $750 million in late 2023 at an $18 billion valuation.

In early 2025, Lightspeed Venture Partners led a $3.5 billion round that valued Anthropic at more than $60 billion.

Series F, G and H

Iconiq led a $13 billion Series F round in late 2025 at a $183 billion valuation. In early 2026, GIC and Coatue Management led a $30 billion Series G round at $380 billion.

The biggest funding round came in May, when Anthropic raised $65 billion in Series H at a $965 billion valuation. Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital led the round, with Amazon contributing $5 billion.

Anthropic's run-rate revenue has since grown from $47 billion at the time of Series H to around $81 billion by the end of October, according to its IPO filing.

2.headline: Crystal Crop Protection IPO opens tomorrow; check latest GMP, lot size, timeline and key details here
2.heading: Crystal Crop Protection IPO opens tomorrow; check latest GMP, lot size, timeline and key details here
2.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of the agrochemicals company, Crystal Crop Protection, is set to open for subscription on Wednesday, November 18.
2.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of the agrochemicals company, Crystal Crop Protection, is set to open for subscription on Wednesday, November 18.

The Rs 455.49-crore IPO will remain open for three days and close on November 20. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 259-272 per equity share. At the upper end of the price band, the company is seeking a valuation of approximately Rs 4,438 crore.

Ahead of the issue opening, the grey market premium (GMP) of Crystal Crop Protection has moderated from the levels seen last week.

Read Also: Rs 30 LPA in Japan or Rs 4.2 LPA in India? Fresher techie questions whether moving abroad is worth it

In the grey market, Crystal Crop Protection shares were commanding a premium of around Rs 13 per share on November 17, according to data from InvestorGain.

At this premium, the estimated listing price works out to around Rs 285 per share, compared with the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 272. This indicates a potential listing gain of approximately 4.78 percent.

The grey market premium has declined from Rs 45 per share on November 13, when the estimated listing gain stood at around 16.5 percent.

However, the GMP is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment and does not guarantee listing gains. It can fluctuate depending on market conditions and should not be considered a prediction of the actual listing price.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 354.77 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 37.03 lakh equity shares aggregating to approximately Rs 100.71 crore.

The fresh issue proceeds will go to the company, while the OFS component will allow promoter Ankur Aggarwal to sell part of his shareholding. The proceeds from the OFS will go to the selling shareholder rather than the company.

The company plans to use the proceeds from the fresh issue primarily to repay or prepay certain outstanding borrowings of the company and its material subsidiary, Saffire Crop Science. The funds will also support inorganic growth through acquisitions, strategic initiatives and general corporate purposes.

The lot size for the Crystal Crop Protection IPO is 55 equity shares. Investors can apply for shares in multiples of 55.

At the upper end of the price band, retail investors will need a minimum investment of Rs 14,960 to apply for one lot of 55 shares, excluding applicable charges.

The issue has reserved 50 percent of the net offer for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), 35 percent for retail individual investors and 15 percent for non-institutional investors (NIIs).

Check IPO News Here

The basis of allotment is expected to be finalised on November 23. The initiation of refunds and credit of shares to successful applicants' demat accounts are scheduled for November 25.

Crystal Crop Protection shares are tentatively scheduled to list on the BSE and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on November 26.

About Crystal Crop Protection

Established in 1994, Crystal Crop Protection is an agricultural solutions company with its corporate office in New Delhi. Its business portfolio spans crop protection products, seeds and other agricultural solutions.

The company manufactures and markets a range of crop protection products, including herbicides, fungicides and insecticides. Its portfolio also includes natural crop solutions such as bio-protectants, bio-stimulants, liquid fertilisers, plant growth regulators and micronutrients.

In addition, Crystal Crop Protection offers seeds for field crops, vegetables and flowers, catering to different agricultural requirements.
